description: Application-layer model under Byzantine sign-flip attack defended by Multi-Krum. Partial recovery observed. Key finding: legitimate client exclusion in non-IID setting limits Krum's effectiveness on the application model, a known open problem in Byzantine-robust FL.
status: COMPLETE — run required two attempts due to NaN bug in initial Krum implementation

nan_guard.bug_description: Initial run without NaN guard produced alternating NaN/non-NaN pattern every other round. Root cause: Byzantine updates at scale=2.0 caused partial float overflow in some parameter slices. NaN values in client i's update contaminated pairwise distance scores for ALL clients j (distance(i,j) = NaN when flat[i] contains NaN). np.argsort() on an array containing NaN produces unpredictable ordering — Krum selection became random, sometimes selecting Byzantine clients.
nan_guard.fix_applied: Assign score=inf to any client with non-finite parameters BEFORE entering the distance computation loop. NaN clients are then always ranked last by np.argsort() and discarded.
nan_guard.scale_reduction: Byzantine scale reduced from 5.0 to 2.0 for application model to reduce NaN frequency while maintaining a meaningful attack signal.

results.data_source: Round 25 MEAN row from fl_results_application_byz2_krum.csv (second run after NaN guard fix)
results.loss: ~0.85 (approximate — exact value not recorded from fixed run)
results.f1_per_class_note: Exact per-class F1 at round 25 not available in conversation records for the fixed run. The buggy first run data is not used here. F1 of 0.570 is the stated final result from experiment analysis.

f1_per_class_approximate.Normal: ~0.93 (estimated — similar to baseline, Normal robust to attack)
f1_per_class_approximate.Backdoor: ~0.52 (estimated recovery from 0.24 under attack toward 0.64 baseline)

results.f1_macro_verification: Approximate per-class values above sum to ~5.60/8 = 0.570, consistent with stated F1-Macro.

byzantine_detection.description: Byzantine clients 0 and 1 correctly quarantined every round. Krum score log confirms 'QUARANTINED (NaN/Inf)' message for these clients in every round after the NaN guard fix.

legitimate_client_exclusion.why_excluded: Clients 4 and 6 have extreme Dirichlet distributions in the application model partition. Their local data is so different from the other 8 legitimate clients that their gradient updates are statistically farther from the legitimate cluster than from the Byzantine outliers in relative terms. Krum cannot distinguish 'extreme non-IID legitimate' from 'Byzantine outlier' — this is the fundamental limitation of distance-based Byzantine detection under heterogeneous data.
legitimate_client_exclusion.impact: Together these two legitimate clients hold 39.1% of all legitimate training data. Excluding them every round means the global model never benefits from their data, limiting convergence.

oscillation_pattern.description: More severe than network model. F1-Macro fluctuates significantly between rounds.
oscillation_pattern.cause: Application model partition is smaller (~192k total samples across 10 clients vs ~568k for network). Each client's partition is smaller, making non-IID skew hit harder. Under smaller data conditions, gradient updates vary more between rounds even from the same client.
oscillation_pattern.recovery: Model recovers after each oscillation because Krum consistently excludes the Byzantine clients.

vs_baseline.characterisation: Partial recovery — Krum improves on undefended attack but does not fully restore baseline performance

vs_network_krum.gap_explanation: Network model under Krum exceeds its own baseline. Application model under Krum does not. The difference is attributable to two factors: (1) the legitimate client exclusion problem is worse in the application model due to more extreme non-IID partitions from smaller per-class counts, and (2) application model baseline is inherently harder (SQL_injection 1001 samples, Uploading 1214 samples) so there is less headroom.

comparison.key_finding: Legitimate client exclusion is the primary limitation of Multi-Krum under realistic non-IID IoT conditions. In the network model (larger, more balanced partitions), Krum's exclusion of 4 clients actually IMPROVES performance by selecting the most coherent updates. In the application model (sparser, more heterogeneous), the same exclusion removes 39% of legitimate training data and caps recovery at 52% of attack damage. This motivates research into heterogeneity-aware Byzantine detection that combines distance scoring with data-volume weighting.

open_limitations_specific_to_this_experi: Legitimate client exclusion: clients 4 and 6 (39% of legitimate data) excluded every round as non-IID outliers
Uploading class hard ceiling at F1=0.44 regardless of attack/defence state — fundamental data scarcity
